goldProduction.title: Gold production (mine-produced)
goldProduction.content:
Mine-produced gold is the metal physically mined and processed at the company's own operations, in kilograms, before any trading or third-party ore purchases.

For Zijin Gold International: this is the overseas gold-mining arm of Zijin Mining, carved out and separately listed in 2025 -- production growth here is the volume side of the thesis, independent of the gold price. H1 FY2026's 27,300kg is already ahead of H1 FY2025's 19,000kg.

What to watch:

  • Output growth versus the reserve/resource base below -- is growth from new mines or faster depletion of existing ones
  • Guidance beats or misses disclosed alongside results

aiscMargin.title: Realized gold price vs AISC
aiscMargin.content:
Realized gold price is the average price actually received per ounce sold. AISC (all-in sustaining cost) is the cost per ounce to mine, process and sustain production -- the industry-standard cash-cost benchmark, inclusive of sustaining capex.

For Zijin Gold International: the gap between the two lines is the cash margin per ounce, and it has widened sharply as spot gold rallied through 2025-26 (H1 FY2026 realized price of $4,643/oz against AISC of $1,678/oz) -- margin here is driven far more by the gold price than by cost control.

What to watch:

  • AISC creeping up (inflation, strip-ratio changes, lower-grade ore) even while price-driven margin looks strong
  • Margin durability if gold gives back part of the recent rally

goldReserves.title: Gold reserves and resources
goldReserves.content:
Reserves (proved + probable) are the contained gold economically mineable at current costs and prices. Resources (measured + indicated + inferred) are the larger, less certain estimate of gold in the ground, including reserves.

For Zijin Gold International: at FY2025, reserves of 917 tonnes and resources of 1,972 tonnes set the mine-life ceiling behind the production chart above -- at the FY2025 mine-produced rate of ~47 tonnes/year, reserves alone imply roughly two decades of current-rate production before further exploration conversion. Only one annual disclosure exists since listing, so this is a level, not yet a trend.

What to watch:

  • Reserve replacement: does next year's figure grow (exploration success, acquisitions) or shrink (depletion without replacement)
  • Resource-to-reserve conversion rate over time

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Zijin Gold International Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
